data.narrative:
eleQtron is a Series A quantum computing company founded by Christof Wunderlich, Michael Johanning, and Jan Henrik Leisse, having raised €50M+ to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 3 public comps (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable valuation method. Using the €50M total raised as a proxy base value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of €100M. Peer-median triangulation proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the quantum computing sector—while 6 same-sector peers exist, none of the narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier) produced the minimum 3 datapoints required for reliable median derivation.

The triangulated valuation range is €85M–€115M, with a median of €100M. This range is derived from a single applicable method, which represents a material constraint on confidence. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.0x multiplier for this specific subsector and the absence of direct peer-stage calibration. Any subsequent valuation refinement should prioritize identification of Series A and Series B quantum computing comps with disclosed valuations or comparable financing terms.
